sections.title: Describing habits
sections.content:
Advanced vocabulary for talking about regular behaviours:
• ingrained — deeply fixed habit. Old habits are deeply ingrained and hard to break.
• ritual — a regular routine done in a specific way. His morning coffee ritual takes exactly fifteen minutes.
• compulsive — resulting from an irresistible urge. Compulsive checking of social media wastes valuable time.
• habitual — done regularly as a habit. She's a habitual early riser, up at 5 a.m. every day.
• kick a habit — stop doing something harmful. He's trying to kick his smoking habit.

sections.title: Change and adaptation
sections.content:
Discussing personal transformation:
• transition — the process of changing. The transition from school to university can be challenging.
• adapt — adjust to new conditions. Humans are remarkably good at adapting to change.
• overhaul — examine thoroughly and make changes. The education system needs a complete overhaul.
• embrace — accept enthusiastically. She embraced the opportunity to work abroad.
• reluctant — unwilling to change. He was reluctant to adopt new technology.

exercises.question: A habit so deeply fixed it's hard to change is:
exercises.explanation: Ingrained means firmly fixed or established; difficult to change.

exercises.question: To stop a harmful habit is to:
exercises.explanation: Kick a habit means to stop doing something that is harmful or addictive.

exercises.question: Thoroughly examining and changing a system is an:
exercises.explanation: An overhaul is a thorough examination and repair or renovation.

exercises.question: Someone unwilling to accept change is:
Adjusting to new conditions or environments is to:
exercises.explanation: Adapt means to adjust to new conditions or environment.

exercises.question: Behaviour driven by an irresistible urge is:
exercises.explanation: Compulsive means resulting from or relating to an irresistible urge.

exercises.question: Accepting something new with enthusiasm is to:
exercises.explanation: Embrace means to accept or support something willingly and enthusiastically.

exercises.question: The process of changing from one state to another is a:
exercises.explanation: A transition is the process of changing from one state or condition to another.
